title: EC3 weak-disposition batch 5: source effects and current evidence
selection: IDs #432, #438, #468, #482, #494, #513, #518, #522, #549, #593 from the literal-mention-only discovery crosswalk. The crosswalk is a locator aid, not a coverage verdict.
source_method: Inspected EC3 annotation objects, including /Subj, /Contents, /IRT and page placement, against the printed text and nearby table/paragraph. Physical PDF page and printed footer are both given. Assertions below refer to test bodies and their actual consumer route.

features.source_location: EC3 physical p.474 / printed p.459, Table 161 /S; StrikeOut obj 4800 with Caret obj 4801, and StrikeOut 4804 with Caret 4805. Strike rectangles cover the printed 'ZZ'/'zz'; replacement contents are 'AZ'/'az'.
features.effective_effect: The EC3 annotation layer preserves both the #432 AA-to-AZ replacement and #593 higher repeated-letter insertions, but subsequent official issue history resolves their conflict: #432 was reopened, lost its ISO-approved label, was marked duplicate and closed completed; #593 received PDF TWG agreement and was closed completed. These events occurred in 2025, before ADR0601.
features.ledger_code_assertions: Current committed finding 2038-D03 records the official status history and a passing public QueryPageLabel→host PageEntry AA/BB assertion (wave4). `crates/viewer-host/tests/page_label_second_block_audit.rs::repeated_page_label_reaches_the_public_page_list` asserts AA at page 27 and BB at page 28. `page_label.rs::letters_repeat_rather_than_carrying` tests the same arithmetic; the source comment and ADR0601 still claim an unresolved conflict.
features.verdict: No current behavior defect: retain D03 and the repeated-letter behavior. The historic EC3 annotations are stale relative to official issue history. ADR0601 postdates that resolution and its unresolved-conflict premise should be corrected; no duplicate finding or test is needed.

features.source_location: EC3 physical p.45 / printed p.30, §7.3.5 NOTE 2; Text annotation obj 1505, no strike/replacement.
features.effective_effect: Informative note explains that #xx escaping permits different textual spellings for the same decoded PDF Name bytes.
features.ledger_code_assertions: The lexer expands #xx escapes before name identity is used. `crates/pdf-syntax/tests/literal_strings_names_audit.rs::name_escapes_are_expanded_before_binary_identity_is_compared` compares escaped and literal spellings at the byte level; adjacent name tests cover escaping boundaries.
features.verdict: The note states an existing syntax rule; direct byte-identity assertions exercise it. No additional behavioral gap found.

features.source_location: EC3 physical p.558 / printed p.543, Table 234 /I; StrikeOut obj 5755 threaded to Caret obj 5756. The replacement inserts the selected-index-array description and the case where Opt entries have different labels but the same export value.
features.effective_effect: The corrected /I prose is no longer restricted to MultiSelect fields and the old array-/V trigger is deleted. It describes sorted zero-based selected Opt indices and requires /I for options with different display names but the same export value. The following text preserves /V precedence only when V and I identify different items.
features.ledger_code_assertions: Committed finding 2038-B26 tracks `viewer-core/tests/duplicate_choice_labels_spec_audit.rs::duplicate_labels_keep_both_array_selected_indices`. The exact-xref public Query::Fields test uses distinct exports x/y with repeated display name Twin, V [(Twin)(Twin)] and agreeing I [0 1]; it fails [0] vs [0,1]. The distinct-label and single-index controls pass in choices-wave20.log. This is a V-array multiplicity issue, not the specific #468 mandatory same-export/different-name case.
features.verdict: Retain B26 with source qualification: V arrays contain selected item names (second Opt-pair member), and the file has two selected names plus indices that describe the same two items. Do not claim #468 mandates I for this fixture or that this is the erratum-specific trigger. Do not create another draft.

features.source_location: EC3 physical p.839 / printed p.824, Table 402 /URLs row; StrikeOut obj 7996 threaded to Caret obj 7997. The row describes URL entries as URL file-specification dictionaries whose /F is an RFC 3986 URL string. Parent checked Strike7996 QuadPoints: old embedded-file or URL specification phrase is wholly replaced.
features.effective_effect: The replacement removes the embedded-file-specification alternative from URLs: every element is a URL file-spec dictionary, FS /URL and PDFDocEncoded F limited to RFC3986. This narrows the permitted producer form; it is not just an added alternative. Output-intent processing remains optional, and conditional consumer behavior must be evaluated separately.
features.ledger_code_assertions: Ledger §14.11.5 and `crates/pdf-model/src/file_spec.rs` retain FS /URL and its /F string; URL specifications are not resolved against a local base. `output_intents_current` identifies the separate conditional consumer rule: if an output intent is respected, a page-level one takes priority even when its referenced profile is unavailable; its page/catalog test currently fails by borrowing the catalog profile. That failure is about scope precedence and does not prove remote URL fetching is mandatory.
features.verdict: URL syntax is represented; no unconditional network-fetch requirement follows from this correction. Preserve the conditional profile-reference/output-intent boundary and do not call Table 402 producer-facing only: consumers that choose to honor the referenced intent may need this data. Existing page-versus-catalog defect is separately evidenced in output_intents_current.

features.source_location: EC3 physical p.41 / printed p.26, Table 3 octal row; StrikeOut obj 1489 threaded to Caret obj 1490, replacing the row text with 'Byte with value ddd in octal.'
features.effective_effect: Clarifies that a three-digit octal escape denotes a byte value, not an abstract character code.
features.ledger_code_assertions: The literal-string lexer emits bytes. `crates/pdf-syntax/tests/literal_strings_names_audit.rs::literal_octal_escapes_take_three_digits_and_keep_only_the_low_byte` asserts exact values for one-, two-, and three-digit forms, overflow, and the following non-octal byte. It uses a valid PDF literal string and directly observes decoded bytes.
features.verdict: Direct source-derived byte assertions cover the corrected meaning; no gap found.

features.source_location: EC3 physical p.504 / printed p.489, Table 179 OpenArrow row; Text annotation obj 5251, no strike/replacement. It explains a clipped table line and repeats the extant description that two short lines meet at an acute angle.
features.effective_effect: Editorial note about table layout; it does not amend the OpenArrow description or line-ending geometry.
features.ledger_code_assertions: `pdf-model/tests/annotations.rs::each_of_table_179_s_line_endings_draws_its_own_shape` checks line-ending shapes, including OpenArrow, through annotation appearance construction.
features.verdict: No normative change is made by this Text note. Existing shape assertions are relevant to the unchanged row; no new behavioral obligation is created.

features.source_location: EC3 physical344/printed329,9.7.3: Strike4225 removes only either; Strike4226 removes or an array of dictionaries and the single-versus-multiple collection qualification. Parent verified each QuadPoint against word boxes.
features.effective_effect: The surviving CMap CIDSystemInfo sentence requires a single dictionary. The former array alternative is removed, not the single-dictionary requirement. Both CMap and CIDFont requirements and Registry/Ordering compatibility survive; Identity CMaps remain compatible with all CIDFonts.
features.ledger_code_assertions: `pdf-font/src/composite.rs::collection_names` reads the descendant font's required CIDSystemInfo. CMap loading primarily consumes code-to-CID mappings; current parser does not expose CMap-stream CIDSystemInfo as a semantic collection field. The archive translator has a separate dictionary-level check. Existing composite-font tests exercise descendant collections and mapping, not the deleted single-vs-array CMap producer encoding.
features.verdict: Producer format is narrowed to one dictionary. No mandatory reader rejection or new semantic representation follows. Current cid_opentype_current already records the array removal correctly. The initial batch5 relaxation wording was an agent misreading, corrected before promotion.

features.source_location: EC3 physical p.73 / printed p.58, Table 15 note; Text obj 1839 says /Size does not decrease in incremental updates. Related Text obj 1958 is physical p.81 / printed p.66 after a Caret obj 1956 updating Table 17's /Prev cross-reference; it repeats the same note.
features.effective_effect: Informative NOTE about writer output across incremental updates, not an amended /Size table requirement or new reader rejection rule.
features.ledger_code_assertions: Xref parsing uses /Size for allocation/section bounds and already tolerates incremental sections; current `/Size` policy/departure is explicitly discussed in ADR 0724 and the xref-stream audit. The note does not independently prescribe how a reader repairs or rejects a decreasing value.
features.verdict: Do not elevate this NOTE to a reader SHALL. Preserve the separately recorded /Size policy/departure; no new behavioral test follows from the note alone.

features.source_location: EC3 physical p.187 / printed p.172, §8.5.3.1; StrikeOut obj 3297 threaded to Caret obj 3298 replaces 'generate an error' with 'be ignored' for a painting operator when no current path exists.
features.effective_effect: Effective reader behavior is explicit: ignore that painting operator when there is no current path; this is distinct from §8.5.2.1 current-point behavior.
features.ledger_code_assertions: `crates/pdf-model/tests/undefined_painting_ignored.rs::undefined_painting_operators_are_ignored_and_do_not_consume_the_next_path` opens an exact-xref file, compares with a clean control, checks that the later valid Fill is observed, Stroke is absent, and the unsupported-operator list stays empty.
features.verdict: Strong direct consumer assertion for the corrected rule. Retain ADR 0548's distinction between the amended no-path painting case and the unchanged current-point case; no gap found.
